title: Finite-Time Chaos Diagnostics and Noise-Induced Basin Merging in a Two-Dimensional Map
summary: Real-world systems, from climate models to power grids, often fluctuate due to sensor noise, drift, or environmental variability, yet standard chaos diagnostics assume fixed parameters and asymptotic horizons. We introduce a finite-time framework for two-dimensional maps under independent, identically distributed parameter noise. First, we prove that the maximal finite-time Lyapunov exponent converges, after centering and scaling, to a Gaussian law whose mean and variance depend explicitly on the map's Jacobian statistics.
